reason: Section 93 states the access and measurement powers of a land surveyor during a boundary survey together with the limit that unnecessary damage must not be done.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Surveyor entry, line-clearing and damage limits
proposedGroups.reason: The target is one rule giving surveyors access and measurement powers while limiting unnecessary damage.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what a land surveyor may do while carrying out a boundary survey and the damage limit on those powers.

reason: Section 94 states one narrow rule that a boundary survey under the Act is limited to external boundaries.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: External-boundaries-only survey rule
proposedGroups.reason: The target contains a single limitation on the scope of a boundary survey.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that a boundary survey under the Act is of external boundaries only.

reason: Section 95 is repeal-only and contains no current operative study content.
Section 96 is repeal-only and contains no current operative study content.
Section 97 is repeal-only; the trailing structural heading does not add operative study content.
Section 98 is one royalty-liability rule with an exception where the person is liable for tax under the Metallic Minerals Tax Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Mining lease royalties and Metallic Minerals Tax Act exception
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections determine when a person who obtains or takes minerals under a mining lease must pay royalties and when the tax liability exception applies.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who must pay royalties for minerals taken under a mining lease and when the Metallic Minerals Tax Act exception applies.

reason: Section 99 separates royalty payment due dates from the Lieutenant-Governor in Council power to suspend royalty requirements for better management of mines and minerals.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Royalty due dates for coal and other royalties
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 99(1) sets monthly due dates for coal royalties and quarterly due dates for other royalties.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when coal royalties and other royalties are due and payable.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Suspension of royalty payment requirements
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 99(2) separately authorizes suspending royalty payment requirements for up to ten years.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the requirement to pay royalties may be suspended and the maximum suspension period.

reason: Section 100 contains a collection framework with two teachable parts: interest/debt/action recovery and certificate-based judgment enforcement after default.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Interest, Crown debt and court action for unpaid royalties, charges or rent
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 100(1) to 100(4) address interest, Crown debt status, recovery by action and costs in that action.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how unpaid royalty, charge or rent amounts bear interest, become Crown debts and may be recovered by action.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister certificate and judgment enforcement after default
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 100(5) to 100(8) set the certificate, demand, filing, judgment and costs process after default.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a Minister certificate for unpaid royalty, charge or rent becomes enforceable as a Court judgment.

reason: Section 101 is a single rule about the form, signature authority and prescribed fee required for a transfer of a mining lease or interest.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Transfer form, signature and fee for mining lease interests
proposedGroups.reason: The target states the required form, signature and fee for transferring a mining lease or an interest in a mining lease.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the form, signature and fee requirements for transferring a mining lease or interest.

reason: Section 101.1 is a focused mineral-claim transfer rule covering registration on payment of a fee and the Recorder’s power to require production of transfer authority.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Mineral claim transfer and production of transfer authority
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections together cover transfer by registry registration, the Recorder’s inspection request and the duty to produce the requested instrument without delay.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a mineral claim is transferred and when transfer authority must be produced for inspection.

reason: Section 102 separates ordinary mining-lease instrument execution and consent requirements from a special filing rule for bank security instruments.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Execution, authorization and Minister consent for mining lease instruments
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 102(1) and 102(2) set execution, verification, agent authorization and Minister consent requirements for instruments affecting a mining lease.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the execution, agent authorization and consent requirements before the Recorder receives a mining lease instrument.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Filing bank security instruments affecting mineral claims or mining leases
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 102(3) separately specifies what must be filed when a mineral claim, mining lease or interest is assigned or transferred as bank security.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what must be filed with the Recorder for bank security affecting a mineral claim, mining lease or interest.

reason: Section 103 gives one priority-protection rule making unregistered or unrecorded instruments void against later valuable purchasers or transferees without actual notice.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Effect of failing to register or record instruments

evidenceText: void as against a subsequent purchaser or transferee

proposedGroups.reason: The target is a single rule about the effect of not registering or recording an instrument affecting a mineral claim or mining lease.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when an instrument affecting a mineral claim or mining lease is void against a subsequent purchaser or transferee.

reason: Section 104 states one notice rule: recording or registration of an instrument gives notice to later claimants despite proof defects.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Recording or registration as notice despite proof defects

evidenceText: notwithstanding any defect in the proof

proposedGroups.reason: The target is a single rule about the notice effect of recording or registration.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the notice effect of recording or registering an instrument under the Act.

reason: Section 105 states one priority rule, subject to section 51, comparing priority of registration or recording with actual notice of a prior instrument.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Priority of registration or recording and actual notice

evidenceText: priority of registration or recording prevails
actual notice of the prior instrument

proposedGroups.reason: The target is a single rule about registration or recording priority and actual notice.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when priority of registration or recording prevails over a prior instrument.

reason: Section 106 separates the authentication and evidentiary requirements for non-ordinary transfers from the Recorder’s duty to enter the entitled person in the records.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Statement, consent and evidence for death, bankruptcy, insolvency or other transfers
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 106(1) and 106(2) state the verified statement, Minister consent for mining leases and supporting documents required for specified transfers.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the statement, consent and evidence required for transfers by death, bankruptcy, insolvency or other non-ordinary means.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Recorder entry of person entitled under transfer
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 106(3) separately directs the Recorder to enter the name of the person entitled under the transfer when the required materials are received.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what the Recorder must do after receiving the required transfer statement, consent and documents.

reason: Section 107 separates address information required on applications and transfers from the legal effect and substitution of addresses for service.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Address information required before filing or recording mining lease applications and transfers
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 107(1) and 107(3) set the residence and post office address information required on applications, transfers and assignments before filing or recording.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the address information required before mining lease applications, transfers or assignments may be filed or recorded.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Address for service and substituted New Brunswick service person
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 107(2) and 107(4) to 107(6) address registered-mail service, substitution of a resident service person and the effect of service.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how address for service and substituted service persons work for mining rights notices, demands and proceedings.

reason: Section 108 contains three distinct topics: rights that claims or leases do not confer, duties to minimize injury and avoid interference, and Board cancellation for unauthorized land use.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Rights not conferred by mineral claims or mining leases
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 108(1) to 108(3) list possession, surface-material and non-mineral-taking rights that a mineral claim or mining lease does not confer.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which possession, surface-material and non-mineral-taking rights are not conferred by a mineral claim or mining lease.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Least injurious land use and non-interference with other resource operations
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 108(4) and 108(5) impose the least-injurious-use duty and prohibit interference with operations under specified Acts.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the least-injurious-use duty and the non-interference rule for other resource operations.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Board hearing, cancellation and withdrawal for unauthorized land use
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 108(6) and 108(7) provide for a Board hearing, cancellation and withdrawal where land is used for an unauthorized purpose.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how unauthorized use of claim, lease or mine land can lead to a Board hearing, cancellation and withdrawal.

reason: Section 109 is too broad for one unit because it covers private-property contact and permission, substitute routes when contact or agreement fails, environmental security, consent-protected lands, and repeat/exception rules.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Private-property contact, notice, agreement and Recorder permission before planned work
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 109(1) to 109(3) state the default personal-contact path and alternatives where contact or agreement with the owner has not been achieved.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the private-property contact, notice, agreement, security and Recorder permission rules before planned work.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Reclamation program, security, owner copy and waiting period for private-property work
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 109(3.1) to 109(3.5) cover Minister-required reclamation programs and security, decision factors, delivery of the program to the owner, a sixty-day waiting period and written consent to earlier commencement.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when private-property work may require a reclamation program and security and what delivery and waiting-period rules follow.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Consent-protected lands for private-property damage or interference
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 109(4) lists lands where actual damage or interference cannot occur without the specified consent.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which private lands require specific consent before causing damage or interference with use and enjoyment.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Staking exception and repeat requirements for planned work
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 109(5) and 109(6) address the staking-only exception and when the notice and related steps must be repeated each year or after significant change.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the staking-only exception and when private-property planned-work steps must be repeated.
